```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Same made-up Nebraska data as last week. Still not real.
# rio imports the data and tidyverse does the data work.
pacman::p_load(rio, tidyverse)
```

# Read in the data

```{r}
# Data is read from the R Study Group folder.
# If your EDV drive letter is different than K: you will need to change it.
linelist <- import("K:/R Study Group/Trenton/Ch12 Pivot/pivot_demo_data.xlsx")

head(linelist)
```

# group_by and summarise

```{r}
# group_by does nothing visible by itself. It just tells R how to split the rows.
# summarise then boils each group down to one row.
# n() counts the rows in the group. mean() averages a column.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd) %>%
  summarise(cases = n(), mean_age = mean(age))
```

```{r}
# You can group by more than one column. One row per LHD and sex.
# NOTE: this is the long format from last week, just with more columns.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd, sex) %>%
  summarise(cases = n(), mean_age = mean(age), max_age = max(age))
```

# count is the shortcut

```{r}
# count does the group_by and summarise(n()) in one step.
# Same numbers as above minus the ages.
linelist %>%
  count(lhd, sex)
```

# Adding a column per group

```{r}
# mutate after group_by keeps every row but calculates within the group.
# Here each case gets the mean age of its own LHD.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd) %>%
  mutate(lhd_mean_age = mean(age)) %>%
  head()
```

# Filtering per group

```{r}
# Oldest case in each LHD. Without group_by this would just be the oldest case overall.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd) %>%
  filter(age == max(age))
```

# ungroup when done

```{r}
# Grouping sticks to the data until you ungroup. Easy to forget.
# NOTE: look at the Groups line at the top of the output above vs here.
linelist %>%
  group_by(lhd) %>%
  mutate(lhd_mean_age = mean(age)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  head()
```
